# API reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/dev/gen_api_reference.py. Do not edit: change the docstring, then regenerate. -->

This file is generated from the code's signatures and docstrings: edit the docstring, then run `python scripts/dev/gen_api_reference.py`. `tests/unit/test_api_reference_fresh.py` fails when this file is stale.

It lists the public Python API: every public method of `IRISGraphEngine` and `IRISGraphOperators` with its signature and the first paragraph of its docstring, the exceptions a caller can catch, and the `IVG_*` environment variables the code reads. The whole docstring (for example `help(IRISGraphEngine.execute_cypher)`) describes the parameters; the [User Guide](USER_GUIDE.md) says how to do a task.

Cypher procedures (`CALL ivg.*`, `CALL gds.*`) are not Python methods, so they are not listed here. The User Guide's [Cypher procedures](USER_GUIDE.md#cypher-procedures) table gives the centrality, PageRank and path procedures' arguments, options and YIELD columns; [Communities](COMMUNITIES.md#cypher-procedures) gives the community procedures'.

Within each group, entries are in alphabetical order.

## `IRISGraphEngine`

`from iris_vector_graph import IRISGraphEngine`

A property graph in one IRIS namespace and IVG Schema: Cypher, node and edge writes, vector and text search, graph algorithms, temporal edges, snapshots and RDF, over the `Graph_KG` tables and `^KG`.

Its methods are grouped by the mixin class that defines them.

### Construction and connection

Building an engine and reaching its connection. Defined in `IRISGraphEngine` (`iris_vector_graph/engine.py`).


The engine's DB-API connection. Reading it is a database access: while the namespace refuses this engine (its IVG Schema was set up by an earlier release and not upgraded) it raises `IVGSchemaError` instead.

### Queries

Cypher, AQL and two-hop counts. Defined in `QueryMixin` (`iris_vector_graph/_engine/query.py`).

#### `execute_aql`

```python
def execute_aql(aql: str, bind_vars: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None) -> 'IVGResult'
```

Run an ArangoDB AQL query by translating it to Cypher and running that.

#### `execute_cypher`

```python
def execute_cypher(
    cypher_query: str,
    parameters: Dict[str, Any] = None,
    read_only: bool = False,
    procedures: Dict[str, Any] = None,
    raise_on_error: bool = False,
) -> 'IVGResult'
```

Run a Cypher query and return its rows as an `IVGResult`. A read the native executor supports runs over `^KG` (on by default; the engine's `native_cypher=False` or `IVG_NATIVE_CYPHER=0` turns it off); every other query is translated to IRIS SQL. Writes (CREATE, MERGE, SET, DELETE) change the graph unless `read_only=True`. A failed statement comes back with `IVGResult.error` set and no rows, unless `raise_on_error=True`.

```python
def khop2_count_fast(node_id: str, predicate: str = '') -> int
```

### Vector, text and index search

Vector search, the BM25, IVF, PLAID and VecIndex indexes, and the index registry. Defined in `VectorMixin` (`iris_vector_graph/_engine/vector.py`).

#### `bm25_build`

```python
def bm25_build(
    name: str,
    text_props: list,
    k1: float = 1.5,
    b: float = 0.75,
    *,
    graph: Optional[str] = None,
) -> dict
```

Build a BM25 index over one graph's nodes (FR-009). Each node's document is the text of its `text_props` properties, lower-cased and split into words, with 77 English stopwords ("a", "and", "at", "for", "the" ...; `Graph.KG.BM25Index.InitStopwords`) left out of documents and queries alike, so they count in neither `avgdl` nor a score (4.6.0 R225); `k1` and `b` are the BM25 parameters. Writes the index (replacing one of the same name), records it in this engine as type `bm25` for `graph`, and returns `{"indexed", "avgdl", "vocab_size", "graph"}`.

#### `bm25_delete`

```python
def bm25_delete(name: str, doc_id: str) -> bool
```

Remove one document from the BM25 index `name` (writes). Returns True if it was in the index, False if it was not or the index does not exist.

#### `bm25_drop`

```python
def bm25_drop(name: str) -> None
```

Delete the BM25 index `name` and all its postings (writes).

#### `bm25_info`

```python
def bm25_info(name: str) -> dict
```

Statistics of the BM25 index `name`: `N` (documents), `avgdl`, `vocab_size`, `graph`, `schema` and `type` (`"bm25"`); only `type` when it does not exist. An index built before graphs were recorded reports `graph` as `""`, the default graph's value, although it covers every graph. Read-only.

#### `bm25_insert`

```python
def bm25_insert(name: str, doc_id: str, text: str) -> bool
```

Add or replace one document in the BM25 index `name` (writes). Returns True when the document is in the index afterwards, False when `text` has no indexable tokens (a replace with such text removes it). Raises for a schema-1 index or one being upgraded; see `bm25_upgrade`.

#### `bm25_search`

```python
def bm25_search(
    name: str,
    query: str,
    k: int = 10,
    max_df_fraction: float = 0.0,
    report: bool = False,
)
```

Top-k documents of the BM25 index `name` for `query`, as `(id, score)` pairs, highest first (a dict with the pairs under `results` when `report=True`). Read-only; the index covers the graph it was built for.

#### `bm25_upgrade`

```python
def bm25_upgrade(name: str) -> dict
```

Convert a schema-1 BM25 index to schema 2 (spec 044 amendment, ADR-0007).

#### `create_index`

```python
def create_index(config, replace: bool = False) -> 'Index'
```

Register an index described by an `IndexConfig` and return its `Index` handle.

#### `edge_vector_search`

```python
def edge_vector_search(
    query_embedding,
    top_k: int = 10,
    score_threshold: float = None,
    *,
    graph: Optional[str] = None,
    model_key: Optional[str] = None,
) -> List[dict]
```

Nearest edges in one graph, from that graph's own edge route (spec 230). Returns up to `top_k` dicts with keys `s`, `p`, `o_id` and `score`, highest cosine score first; `score_threshold` drops edges scoring below it. Read-only.


#### `ivf_build`

```python
def ivf_build(
    name: str,
    nlist: int = 256,
    metric: str = 'cosine',
    batch_size: int = 10000,
    build_batch_size: int = 500,
    node_ids: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    *,
    graph: Optional[str] = None,
    model_key: Optional[str] = None,
) -> dict
```

Build an IVF index over one graph's vectors in one routed table (spec 227). Reads the `(graph, model_key)` route's vectors (or only `node_ids`), clusters them client-side into `min(nlist, n)` cells with mini-batch k-means (needs numpy and scikit-learn), and writes the index `name` with `Graph.KG.IVFIndex`, replacing one of that name. Records it in this engine for `graph` and returns `{"nlist", "dim", "metric", "indexed"}`. Raises `ValueError` when the pair has no route or the route holds no vectors.

Remove `node_id`'s vector from the IVF index `name` (writes). Returns True if it was there.

#### `ivf_search`

```python
def ivf_search(name: str, query: list, k: int = 10, nprobe: int = 8) -> list
```

Approximate nearest neighbours of `query` in the IVF index `name`, scanning the `nprobe` cells whose centroids are closest. Returns up to `k` `(node_id, score)` tuples, best first, or `[]` when the index does not exist. Read-only; the index covers the graph it was built for.

#### `kg_KNN_VEC`

```python
def kg_KNN_VEC(
    query_vector: str,
    k: int = 50,
    label_filter: Optional[str] = None,
    dtype: Optional[str] = None,
    *,
    graph: Optional[str] = None,
    model_key: Optional[str] = None,
) -> List[Tuple[str, float]]
```

Nearest neighbours inside one graph (spec 227): up to `k` `(node_id, cosine)` pairs, highest first, from the embedding table the `(graph, model_key)` pair is routed to. `query_vector` is a JSON array string, or a node ID whose stored vector is used (that node is left out of the answer); `label_filter` keeps nodes with that label. Read-only.

#### `kg_NEIGHBORHOOD_EXPANSION`

```python
def kg_NEIGHBORHOOD_EXPANSION(
    entity_list: List[str],
    expansion_depth: int = 1,
    confidence_threshold: int = 500,
    *,
    graph: Optional[str] = None,
) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]
```

One-hop outgoing edges of the seed nodes whose qualifier `confidence` is at least `confidence_threshold`, in one graph. Returns dicts with keys `source`, `predicate`, `target` and `confidence`, highest confidence first. An edge with no `confidence` qualifier is not returned. `expansion_depth` is accepted and ignored: the expansion is always one hop. Read-only.

#### `kg_RRF_FUSE`

```python
def kg_RRF_FUSE(
    k: int,
    k1: int,
    k2: int,
    c: int,
    query_vector: str,
    query_text: str,
    graph: Optional[str] = None,
) -> List[Tuple[str, float, float, float]]
```

Client-side RRF over a vector leg and a BM25 leg. The vector leg takes `k1` hits from the graph's IVF index or `kg_KNN_VEC`, the BM25 leg `k2` hits for `query_text` (skipped when it is empty); each hit scores `1 / (c + rank)`. Returns up to `k` tuples `(node_id, rrf, vector_score, bm25_score)`, highest `rrf` first. A failed index search is logged at ERROR and the legs not yet searched contribute nothing. Read-only.

#### `kg_TXT`

```python
def kg_TXT(
    query_text: str,
    k: int = 50,
    min_confidence: int = 0,
    *,
    graph: Optional[str] = None,
) -> List[Tuple[str, float]]
```

Full-text search over one graph's rows of the docs table: up to `k` `(node_id, score)` pairs, highest first. The score is the number of times `query_text` occurs in the document (iFind index path), or 1.0 for every match when the namespace has no iFind index and a `LIKE` match on each word is used. Read-only.

#### `kg_VECTOR_GRAPH_SEARCH`

```python
def kg_VECTOR_GRAPH_SEARCH(
    query_vector: str,
    query_text: str = None,
    k: int = 15,
    expansion_depth: int = 1,
    min_confidence: float = 0.5,
    *,
    graph: Optional[str] = None,
) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]
```

Candidates from vector search, their one-hop neighbours and (with `query_text`) text search, in one graph, scored by vector similarity alone. It takes `min(2k, 50)` `kg_KNN_VEC` hits, adds the targets of their edges whose `confidence` qualifier (0 to 1000) is at least `1000 * min_confidence` and the `kg_TXT` hits, keeps `k` of that set in no particular order, and sorts them by `vector_similarity`, which is 0.0 for a node found only by expansion or text. Returns dicts with keys `entity_id`, `combined_score` (equal to `vector_similarity`), `vector_similarity` and `in_graph_expansion`. Read-only.

#### `multi_vector_search`

```python
def multi_vector_search(
    sources: List[dict],
    query_embedding,
    top_k: int = 10,
    fusion: str = 'rrf',
    rrf_k: int = 60,
    *,
    graph: Optional[str] = None,
) -> List[dict]
```

Fuse several vector columns, all within one graph. Each `sources` entry (`table`, `col`, optional `id_col`, `weight`, `return_cols`, `graph`) is searched with `vector_search` for `2 * top_k` rows; `fusion="rrf"` ranks by weighted reciprocal rank (`rrf_k`), any other value by raw score. Returns up to `top_k` dicts. A source that fails is logged and skipped.

### Graph algorithms

Centrality, communities, ranking, walks and the `kg_*` operators. Defined in `AlgorithmsMixin` (`iris_vector_graph/_engine/algorithms.py`).

#### `betweenness_centrality`

```python
def betweenness_centrality(
    sample_size: int = 0,
    direction: str = 'out',
    max_hops: int = 0,
    top_k: int = 10000,
    mem_budget_mb: int = 256,
    progress_callback: Optional[Callable[[int, int], NoneType]] = None,
) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]
```

Betweenness centrality via Brandes (2001) algorithm, one row per node that lies on some shortest path between two others: a node scoring 0 has no row, where `closeness_centrality` and `degree_centrality` list every node with an edge, zeros included, so for the lowest scores count each node with an edge and no row as 0 (`CALL ivg.betweenness` and `gds.betweenness.stream` answer the same rows).

#### `betweenness_centrality_neighborhood`

```python
def betweenness_centrality_neighborhood(
    seed: str,
    hops: int = 2,
    sample_size: int = 200,
    top_k: int = 20,
) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]
```

Betweenness centrality within a node's neighborhood: Brandes on the subgraph induced by the nodes `seed` reaches by out-edges within `hops` hops (the seed included), directed, highest first and ties by id. With `sample_size` at or above the neighbourhood's size it is networkx's `betweenness_centrality(G, normalized=False)` on that subgraph; a smaller one takes that many sources and scales by the size over it.

#### `bfs_vector_rerank`

```python
def bfs_vector_rerank(
    seed: str,
    query_vec: List[float],
    hops: int = 2,
    top_k: int = 10,
    max_buckets: int = 32,
) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]
```

Not implemented on IVG's own store: raises `NotImplementedError`. A hook for a store that has it.

#### `closeness_centrality`

```python
def closeness_centrality(
    formula: str = 'harmonic',
    direction: str = 'out',
    max_hops: int = 0,
    top_k: int = 10000,
    progress_callback: Optional[Callable[[int, int], NoneType]] = None,
) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]
```

Closeness centrality over shortest-path distances from each node (`direction="out"`: the hops to the nodes it reaches). `formula="harmonic"` (the default) is the sum of 1/d over the nodes reached, not normalised (networkx's `harmonic_centrality` on the reversed graph for `"out"`); `"classical"` is (n - 1) / (sum of d) for a node that reaches all n - 1 others, and 0 for one that does not. No other value is accepted (4.6.0 R225). n is `node_count()`: a node with no edge scores 0, and once there is one no node reaches all n - 1 others, so every classical score is 0 (4.6.0 R306; before, such a node had no row and n counted only the nodes with an edge). `"in"` scores the hops from the nodes that reach it, `"both"` the undirected graph (4.6.0 R306: `"both"` answered `"out"`'s scores where `^NKG` answers). Highest first, ties by id.

#### `degree_centrality`

```python
def degree_centrality(
    direction: str = 'out',
    predicate: Optional[str] = None,
    top_k: int = 10000,
    *,
    graph: Optional[str] = None,
) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]
```

Each node's `degree` (its number of edges in `direction`) and `score`, its degree / (n - 1), n being `node_count(graph)`, highest first, ties by id: on 6 nodes a node with 3 out-edges has degree 3 and score 0.6. A node with no edge has a row, degree 0 (4.6.0 R306; before, it had none and n counted only the nodes with an edge). `CALL ivg.degreeCentrality` yields the same two, as `degree` and `score`.

#### `eigenvector_centrality`

```python
def eigenvector_centrality(
    max_iter: int = 30,
    tol: float = 1e-06,
    top_k: int = 10000,
    progress_callback: Optional[Callable[[int, int], NoneType]] = None,
) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]
```

Eigenvector centrality by power iteration on the directed graph: a node's score is the sum of the scores of the nodes with an edge to it, each once however many edges it has to the node (4.6.0 R306: the ObjectScript route counted an edge under each predicate, the ^KG walk each node once), L2-normalised each round, stopping after `max_iter` rounds (1 to 1000; default 30) or when no score moves by more than `tol`. 30 rounds can stop short of convergence, a few hundredths off; `max_iter=1000` with a small `tol` matches networkx's `eigenvector_centrality(G)` on the directed graph (4.6.0 R225). A node with no edge scores 0 (4.6.0 R306: it had no row). Highest first, ties by id.

#### `k_core`

```python
def k_core(
    top_k: int = 10000,
    progress_callback: Optional[Callable[[int, int], NoneType]] = None,
) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]
```

K-core decomposition (Batagelj-Zaversnik 2003, O(V+E)). A node with no edge to another node has coreness 0 (4.6.0 R306: it had no row).

```python
def kg_CDLP(max_iterations: int = 10) -> Dict[str, Any]
```

Communities by label propagation (CDLP), as `{node: community}`. A self-loop is no vote: a node's own label is not counted (4.6.0 R306: a self-loop counted twice for it).

```python
def kg_NEIGHBORS(

    chunk_size: int = 500,
) -> List[str]
```

The node IDs one hop from `source_ids`, along `predicate` edges if given.

#### `kg_PAGERANK`

```python
def kg_PAGERANK(
    seed_entities: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    damping: float = 0.85,
    max_iterations: int = 20,
    bidirectional: bool = False,
    reverse_weight: float = 1.0,
)
```

Global PageRank over the default graph as a list of `(node_id, score)` pairs, highest first, or, with `seed_entities`, personalized PageRank from those nodes as a `{node_id: score}` dict. `damping` is the probability of following an edge rather than restarting. `max_iterations` (20) is a fixed count with no convergence test: 20 can leave scores a few hundredths from converged, so raise it (for example to 200) to compare with networkx's `pagerank(G, weight=None)` (4.6.0 R225). With the Arno library loaded in USER the walk also stops once converged, within about 2e-6 of the fixed count's scores. Every node of the default graph takes part, a node with no edge as one with no out-edge, and the scores sum to 1 over `node_count()` nodes: networkx's `pagerank(G)` (4.6.0 R306; before, a node with no edge had no pair and the scores summed to 1 over the others). Ties go by node id. `kg_PAGERANK(seed_entities=["a"])` returns `kg_PERSONALIZED_PAGERANK(["a"], damping_factor=damping, max_iterations=max_iterations)`: the same walk, stopped after 20 iterations by default where `kg_PERSONALIZED_PAGERANK` allows 100 and stops once converged, so call that one for personalized PageRank. `bidirectional` and `reverse_weight` are accepted and ignored, in both forms: edges are followed in their direction only.

#### `kg_PERSONALIZED_PAGERANK`

```python
def kg_PERSONALIZED_PAGERANK(
    seed_entities: List[str],
    damping_factor: float = 0.85,
    max_iterations: int = 100,
    tolerance: float = 1e-06,
    return_top_k: Optional[int] = None,
    bidirectional: bool = False,
    reverse_edge_weight: float = 1.0,
    *,
    graph: Optional[str] = None,
    exclude_predicates: Optional[List[str]] = None,
) -> Dict[str, float]
```

Personalized PageRank from `seed_entities`, as `{node_id: score}`: networkx's `pagerank(G, alpha=damping_factor, personalization={seed: 1, ...}, tol=tolerance)`, G the graph as a multigraph (an edge under each predicate counts, as does each keyed edge of a multigraph-mode triple). At each step the walk restarts at the seeds (evenly) with probability `1 - damping_factor` and otherwise follows an out-edge chosen evenly; a node with no out-edges hands its score to the seeds, as networkx does, so the scores sum to 1. It stops after `max_iterations` or once the scores' summed change in an iteration is below N \* `tolerance`, N the nodes holding a score (networkx's rule, whose N is every node of the graph). Every route gives this answer: the server walk (`Graph.KG.PageRank.RunJson`) and the Python fallback. Before 4.6.0 (R270) both passed a dangling node's score nowhere, so the scores summed to less than 1, and the server walk stopped once no score moved by 1e-4 whatever `tolerance` said.

```python
def kg_WCC(max_iterations: Optional[int] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]
```

Weakly connected components, as `{node: component}`. Labels propagate until they settle; `max_iterations` is a safety limit on the rounds, and raises `WCC did not converge in n rounds` when it is reached first (before 4.5.2: 100 rounds, then whatever labels it had). With a limit the ObjectScript Owner answers, on the store path too (before 4.6.0 the store ignored the limit). A node with no edge is a component of its own, labelled with itself (4.6.0 R306: it had no entry).

### Sub-engines

Four attributes of an engine group some of its methods by subject. Each method forwards its arguments unchanged to the engine method shown (or, marked `_store.`, to the engine's store).

#### `engine.graph`

Structural graph mutations and queries.

- `bulk_create_edges` calls `bulk_create_edges`
- `bulk_create_nodes` calls `bulk_create_nodes`
- `create_edge` calls `create_edge`
- `create_node` calls `create_node`
- `delete_edge` calls `delete_edge`
- `delete_node` calls `delete_node`
- `delete_nodes_by_prefix` calls `delete_nodes_by_prefix`
- `get_edge_count` calls `get_edge_count`
- `get_labels` calls `get_labels`
- `get_node_count` calls `get_node_count`
- `get_relationship_types` calls `get_relationship_types`
- `is_multigraph` calls `is_multigraph`
- `set_multigraph` calls `set_multigraph`

#### `engine.cypher`

Cypher query execution and adjacency index management.

- `execute_bfs` calls `_store.execute_bfs`
- `execute_cypher` calls `execute_cypher`
- `execute_knn_vec` calls `_store.execute_knn_vec`
- `rebuild_kg` calls `rebuild_kg`
- `rebuild_nkg` calls `rebuild_nkg`
- `sync` calls `sync`

#### `engine.temporal`

Temporal edge graph — event-time writes and window queries.

- `backfill_temporal_structural_rows` calls `backfill_temporal_structural_rows`
- `bulk_create_edges_temporal` calls `bulk_create_edges_temporal`
- `create_edge_temporal` calls `create_edge_temporal`
- `delete_edge_temporal` calls `delete_edge_temporal`
- `drop_temporal_structural_rows` calls `drop_temporal_structural_rows`
- `erase_bare_nodes` calls `erase_bare_nodes`
- `find_burst_nodes` calls `find_burst_nodes`
- `get_bucket_group_targets` calls `get_bucket_group_targets`
- `get_bucket_groups` calls `get_bucket_groups`
- `get_edge_attrs` calls `get_edge_attrs`
- `get_edge_velocity` calls `get_edge_velocity`
- `get_edges_in_window` calls `get_edges_in_window`
- `get_latest_edges` calls `get_latest_edges`
- `get_temporal_aggregate` calls `get_temporal_aggregate`
- `get_temporal_structural` calls `get_temporal_structural`
- `iter_edges_in_window` calls `iter_edges_in_window`
- `list_temporal_structural_opt_outs` calls `list_temporal_structural_opt_outs`
- `purge_raw_before` calls `purge_raw_before`
- `rebuild_temporal_latest` calls `rebuild_temporal_latest`
- `set_temporal_structural` calls `set_temporal_structural`

#### `engine.algorithms`

Graph algorithms — centrality, community detection, ranking.

- `betweenness_centrality` calls `betweenness_centrality`
- `closeness_centrality` calls `closeness_centrality`
- `degree_centrality` calls `degree_centrality`
- `eigenvector_centrality` calls `eigenvector_centrality`
- `execute_k_core` calls `k_core`
- `execute_scc` calls `strongly_connected_components`
- `execute_triangle_count` calls `triangle_count`
- `execute_wcc` calls `kg_WCC`
- `leiden_communities` calls `leiden_communities`
- `pagerank` calls `kg_PAGERANK`

## `IRISGraphOperators`

`from iris_vector_graph.operators import IRISGraphOperators`

The `kg_*` retrieval operators under their older calling conventions.

Defined in `iris_vector_graph/operators.py`.

### Methods

#### `IRISGraphOperators.kg_CDLP`

```python
def kg_CDLP(max_iterations=10)
```

Same as `IRISGraphEngine.kg_CDLP`: communities by label propagation, as `{node: community}`.

#### `IRISGraphOperators.kg_GRAPH_PATH`

```python
def kg_GRAPH_PATH(src_id, pred1, pred2, max_hops=2)
```

Same as `IRISGraphEngine.kg_GRAPH_PATH`: two-hop paths `src_id -pred1-> b -pred2-> c`, one row per step.

#### `IRISGraphOperators.kg_GRAPH_WALK`

```python
def kg_GRAPH_WALK(start_entity, max_depth=3, edge_types=None, max_results=100)
```

Same as `IRISGraphEngine.kg_GRAPH_WALK`: a breadth-first walk outbound from `start_entity`, up to `max_depth` hops.

#### `IRISGraphOperators.kg_GRAPH_WALK_TVF`

```python
def kg_GRAPH_WALK_TVF(start_entity, max_depth=3, edge_types=None, max_results=100)
```

Same as `IRISGraphEngine.kg_GRAPH_WALK_TVF`, the older name of `kg_GRAPH_WALK`.

#### `IRISGraphOperators.kg_KNN_VEC`

```python
def kg_KNN_VEC(query_vector, k=50, label_filter=None, graph=None, model_key=None)
```

Same as `IRISGraphEngine.kg_KNN_VEC`: up to `k` `(node_id, cosine)` pairs nearest `query_vector` in one graph's routed embedding table. `dtype` cannot be passed here; the engine's vector type is used.

#### `IRISGraphOperators.kg_MENTIONS`

```python
def kg_MENTIONS(source_ids, predicate='MENTIONS', direction='out')
```

Same as `IRISGraphEngine.kg_MENTIONS`: the IDs one hop away along `MENTIONS` edges (or `predicate`).

#### `IRISGraphOperators.kg_NEIGHBORHOOD_EXPANSION`

```python
def kg_NEIGHBORHOOD_EXPANSION(*args, **kwargs)
```

Same as `IRISGraphEngine.kg_NEIGHBORHOOD_EXPANSION` (arguments passed through): the seeds' one-hop outgoing edges whose `confidence` qualifier meets the threshold.

#### `IRISGraphOperators.kg_NEIGHBORS`

```python
def kg_NEIGHBORS(source_ids, predicate=None, direction='out', distinct=True, chunk_size=500)
```

Same as `IRISGraphEngine.kg_NEIGHBORS`: the node IDs one hop from `source_ids`, along `predicate` edges if given.

#### `IRISGraphOperators.kg_PAGERANK`

```python
def kg_PAGERANK(
    seed_entities=None,
    damping=0.85,
    max_iterations=20,
    bidirectional=False,
    reverse_weight=1.0,
)
```

Same as `IRISGraphEngine.kg_PAGERANK`: PageRank as `(node_id, score)` pairs, or with `seed_entities` personalized PageRank's `{node_id: score}` dict. `bidirectional` and `reverse_weight` are accepted and not passed on, so the engine's defaults (directed, weight 1.0) always apply.

#### `IRISGraphOperators.kg_PPR`

```python
def kg_PPR(seed_entities, damping=0.85, max_iterations=20)
```

Same as `IRISGraphEngine.kg_PPR`: personalized PageRank from `seed_entities`, as `(node_id, score)` pairs, best first.

#### `IRISGraphOperators.kg_PPR_GUIDED_SUBGRAPH`

```python
def kg_PPR_GUIDED_SUBGRAPH(
    seed_ids,
    ppr_top_k=50,
    top_k=None,
    k_hops=1,
    max_hops=None,
    damping=0.85,
    max_iterations=10,
    edge_types=None,
    max_nodes=5000,
)
```

Same as `IRISGraphEngine.kg_PPR_GUIDED_SUBGRAPH`: the subgraph around the nodes personalized PageRank ranks highest for `seed_ids`. `top_k`, when given, replaces `ppr_top_k`, and `max_hops` replaces `k_hops`.

#### `IRISGraphOperators.kg_RERANK`

```python
def kg_RERANK(top_n, query_vector, query_text)
```

Same as `IRISGraphEngine.kg_RERANK`: the `top_n` best nodes for a vector and a text query, fused by `kg_RRF_FUSE`.

#### `IRISGraphOperators.kg_RRF_FUSE`

```python
def kg_RRF_FUSE(k=50, k1=200, k2=200, c=60, query_vector='[]', query_text='', graph=None)
```

Same as `IRISGraphEngine.kg_RRF_FUSE`, with defaults for every argument: reciprocal-rank fusion of a vector leg and a BM25 leg, as `(node_id, rrf, vector_score, bm25_score)` tuples.

#### `IRISGraphOperators.kg_SUBGRAPH`

```python
def kg_SUBGRAPH(
    seed_ids,
    k_hops=2,
    edge_types=None,
    include_properties=True,
    include_embeddings=False,
    max_nodes=10000,
)
```

Same as `IRISGraphEngine.kg_SUBGRAPH`: the subgraph within `k_hops` of `seed_ids`, as a `SubgraphData`.

#### `IRISGraphOperators.kg_TXT`

```python

```

Same as `IRISGraphEngine.kg_TXT`: full-text search over one graph's documents, as `(node_id, score)` pairs.

#### `IRISGraphOperators.kg_VECTOR_GRAPH_SEARCH`

```python
def kg_VECTOR_GRAPH_SEARCH(
    query_vector,
    query_text=None,
    k=15,
    k_vector=None,
    k_final=None,
    expansion_depth=1,
    min_confidence=0.5,
    graph=None,
)
```

Same as `IRISGraphEngine.kg_VECTOR_GRAPH_SEARCH`: vector hits, their one-hop neighbours and text hits, scored by vector similarity. The engine takes one `k`: it is `k_final` if given, else `k_vector`, else `k`.

#### `IRISGraphOperators.kg_WCC`

```python
def kg_WCC(max_iterations=None)
```

Same as `IRISGraphEngine.kg_WCC`: weakly connected components, as `{node: component}`.

## Exceptions and warnings

The classes a caller can catch, with the import that reaches each and its base classes.

### `AQLParseError`

`from iris_vector_graph import AQLParseError`; subclass of `Exception`.

An AQL query is not valid AQL; `line` and `column` locate the token that stopped the parser.

### `AQLTranslationError`

`from iris_vector_graph import AQLTranslationError`; subclass of `Exception`.

An AQL query parses but uses a construct IVG does not translate to Cypher (a nested `FOR`, `SEARCH`, `K_SHORTEST_PATHS`); `aql_construct` names it.

### `BulkLoadError`

`from iris_vector_graph.exceptions import BulkLoadError`; subclass of `RuntimeError`.

Raised when a bulk-load batch is rejected for anything but a duplicate row.

### `ClassesUnreadable`

`from iris_vector_graph import ClassesUnreadable`; subclass of `RuntimeError`.

The namespace's routines database refuses this user IVG's classes: grant the role `<routines database resource>:R` (ADMIN_GUIDE §3).

### `EmbeddedUnavailableError`

`from iris_vector_graph.embedded import EmbeddedUnavailableError`; subclass of `ImportError`.

Embedded mode asked for in a process that is not inside IRIS.

### `EmbeddingIdentityConflict`

`from iris_vector_graph import EmbeddingIdentityConflict`; subclass of `ValueError`.

Raised when a write's declared embedding identity disagrees with the one recorded for the table in `Graph_KG.embedding_registry` (spec 226, FR-010).

### `EmbeddingsMissingError`

`from iris_vector_graph import EmbeddingsMissingError`; subclass of `PrerequisiteError`.

A vector operation needs embeddings that have not been generated.

### `FHIRGraphError`

`from iris_vector_graph.exceptions import FHIRGraphError`; subclass of `RuntimeError`.

Raised when `Graph.KG.FHIRGraph` answers `{"status": "error"}` (spec 231).

### `GraphWriteError`

`from iris_vector_graph import GraphWriteError`; subclass of `IVGError`, `RuntimeError`.

A data-changing write failed in IRIS; everything it had written is rolled back.

### `IVGClientError`

`from iris_vector_graph import IVGClientError`; subclass of `IVGError`.

The HTTP client could not get an answer: the server refused the API key (401) or the request (403), or every retry failed to connect or timed out. `http_code` is the status, or None when no response came back.

### `IVGError`

`from iris_vector_graph import IVGError`; subclass of `Exception`.

Base class of IVG's own errors: the HTTP client's, and the engine's in `iris_vector_graph.errors`.

### `IVGSchemaError`

`from iris_vector_graph import IVGSchemaError`; subclass of `RuntimeError`.

A namespace's IVG Schema cannot be used as asked: it was set up by an earlier release and not upgraded, or it is recorded under another name than the engine's (FR-006, FR-006a), or setup cannot tell which schema is IVG's.

### `IVGServerError`

`from iris_vector_graph import IVGServerError`; subclass of `IVGError`.

The IVG server answered with an error: a 5xx status on the last retry, or a query result carrying an error (then `http_code` is 200 and `query` is the query that failed).

### `IndexNotBuiltError`

`from iris_vector_graph import IndexNotBuiltError`; subclass of `PrerequisiteError`.

An index exists but contains no entries (build never ran or found nothing).

### `IndexNotFoundError`

`from iris_vector_graph import IndexNotFoundError`; subclass of `PrerequisiteError`.

A named index does not exist yet.

### `IndexNotSyncedError`

`from iris_vector_graph import IndexNotSyncedError`; subclass of `PrerequisiteError`.

Bulk writes happened but the adjacency/acceleration index is stale.

### `NamespaceConsistencyError`

`from iris_vector_graph import NamespaceConsistencyError`; subclass of `ValueError`.

Raised when two IVG components (e.g. engine and vector store) are configured for different IRIS namespaces, which would cause silent cross-namespace read/write asymmetry.

### `NamespaceMismatchWarning`

`from iris_vector_graph import NamespaceMismatchWarning`; subclass of `UserWarning`.

Raised when the engine's configured namespace does not match the live IRIS connection's namespace, or when ^KG globals are not accessible in the connected namespace.

### `NativeMismatch`

`from iris_vector_graph.cypher.native_shadow import NativeMismatch`; subclass of `AssertionError`.

The native executor's answer differs from the SQL path's.

### `NodeNotFoundError`

`from iris_vector_graph import NodeNotFoundError`; subclass of `IVGError`.

A referenced node id does not exist in the graph.

### `ParallelEdgesPresentError`

`from iris_vector_graph.errors import ParallelEdgesPresentError`; subclass of `IVGError`.

A graph cannot leave multigraph mode while a triple still has two edges.

### `PrerequisiteError`

`from iris_vector_graph import PrerequisiteError`; subclass of `IVGError`.

Raised when a required setup step was skipped. Carries a `remedy`.

### `TableNotMappedError`

`IRISGraphEngine.TableNotMappedError`; subclass of `ValueError`.

Raised by `attach_embeddings_to_table` for a label `map_sql_table` has not mapped.

### `TemporalWindowError`

`from iris_vector_graph.exceptions import TemporalWindowError`; subclass of `RuntimeError`.

Raised when a temporal window or latest-event read fails on the server (spec 255, FR-006).

## Environment variables

Every `IVG_*` variable the code in `iris_vector_graph/` and `api/` reads.

### `IVG_ALLOW_FHIR_WRITES`

Default: unset. Read in `iris_vector_graph/api_auth.py`.

With `IVG_READ_ONLY=true`, `true` lets the HTTP server accept POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE on the `/fhir-event` routes, which read-only mode otherwise refuses with 403.

### `IVG_API_KEY`

Default: unset. Read in `iris_vector_graph/_api_key.py`, `iris_vector_graph/cli.py`.

When set, every route of the HTTP servers requires this value in an `X-Api-Key` (or `Authorization: Bearer`) header (`/health` and the OpenAPI pages stay open), a Bolt client must send it as the `credentials` of `HELLO` or `LOGON` before it can run a query, and the `ivg` command-line client sends it (`--api-key`).

### `IVG_ARNO_LIB`

Default: `/usr/irissys/mgr/libarno_callout.so`. Read in `iris_vector_graph/stores/arno_bridge.py`.

Path, on the IRIS server, of the Arno accelerator library. Both loaders take it ahead of the path the namespace recorded at its last load (`^ArnoAccel("lib_path")`) and the default.

### `IVG_ARNO_PROOF`

Default: the proof in the wheel (`iris_vector_graph/_data/arno-reader-proof.json`); in a source checkout, `docs/dev/arno-reader-proof.json`. Read in `iris_vector_graph/arno_readers.py`.

Path of the Arno reader proof: the minimum library reader revision per algorithm at which the Rust reader may answer instead of the ObjectScript implementation.

### `IVG_CYPHER_MAX_HOPS`

Default: `10`. Read in `api/routers/cypher.py`.

Largest variable-length hop count the HTTP server's Cypher route accepts; a non-positive or non-numeric value means the default.

### `IVG_CYPHER_SHADOW`

Default: unset. Read in `iris_vector_graph/_engine/query.py`.

`1` runs each native Cypher read on the SQL path too and raises `NativeMismatch` where the answers differ (the engine's `cypher_shadow` attribute does the same for one engine). Doubles the work; for testing.

### `IVG_DISABLE_ALGO_CACHE`

Default: unset. Read in `iris_vector_graph/algo_cache.py`.

`1` turns off the shared algorithm result cache (`^IVG.AlgoCache`); every call computes its answer.

### `IVG_DISABLE_ARNO`

Default: unset. Read in `iris_vector_graph/stores/arno_bridge.py`.

`1` makes IVG act as if the Arno library were absent: algorithms run their ObjectScript or Python implementations.

### `IVG_EDGESCAN`

Default: unset. Read in `iris_vector_graph/cypher/translator.py`.

`1` makes a directed hop on the SQL path join the `Graph_KG.MatchEdges` scan of `^KG` instead of `rdf_edges` (the plan before 4.3.0; about 77 us an edge on a hub).

### `IVG_EMBEDDED_PYTHON`

Default: unset (probe the server). Read in `iris_vector_graph/_engine/class_deploy.py`.

`1` or `0` says whether the IRIS server can run `[ Language = python ]` methods, instead of probing it; class deploy skips the classes that need Embedded Python when it cannot.

### `IVG_FHIR_ALLOWED_BASES`

Default: unset. Read in `iris_vector_graph/cypher_api.py`.

Comma-separated FHIR base URLs the HTTP server may fetch when a Cypher request names `fhir_base_url`, compared exactly (a trailing slash aside). Any other URL is refused; unset, every caller-supplied URL is.

### `IVG_FORCE_CLASS_DEPLOY`

Default: unset. Read in `iris_vector_graph/_engine/class_deploy.py`, `iris_vector_graph/_engine/schema.py`.

`1` makes class deploy load and compile the packaged ObjectScript classes even when the namespace's deploy fingerprint says they are current, and setup create every SQL function and procedure even when its fingerprint says it is unchanged.

### `IVG_GRAPHQL_MAX_DEPTH`

Default: `10`. Read in `api/gql/schema.py`.

Deepest GraphQL query the HTTP server accepts; a non-positive or non-numeric value means the default.

### `IVG_IGNORE_NAMESPACE_CHECK`

Default: unset. Read in `iris_vector_graph/stores/iris_sql_store.py`.

`1` silences the warning logged when `namespace=` names a namespace other than the connection's.

### `IVG_NATIVE_CYPHER`

Default: `1`. Read in `iris_vector_graph/engine.py`.

`0` sends every Cypher read to the SQL path; otherwise the native executor answers the reads it supports. `IRISGraphEngine(native_cypher=False)` does the same for one engine.

### `IVG_NATIVE_PARALLEL_MIN`

Default: `1500`. Read in `iris_vector_graph/engine.py`.

Estimated work (anchors times the sampled fan-out of the first two hops) at which a native read is split across worker processes; `0` always splits, a negative value never does.

### `IVG_NATIVE_ROUTE_MS`

Default: `50`. Read in `iris_vector_graph/engine.py`.

A query shape native answers in less than this many ms is also timed on the SQL path, and the faster path answers it from then on; `0` never times.

### `IVG_PROBE_IDLE_SECONDS`

Default: `30`. Read in `iris_vector_graph/engine.py`.

How long the engine's connection may sit idle before the next Cypher call probes it and reconnects a stale one; `0` probes on every call.

### `IVG_READ_ONLY`

Default: unset. Read in `api/gql/schema.py`, `api/routers/cypher.py`, `iris_vector_graph/api_auth.py`.

`true` makes the HTTP servers refuse writes with 403: mutating Cypher on the Cypher routes, the Neo4j HTTP routes, Bolt and GraphQL, GraphQL mutations, every write method under `/admin/` except `/admin/explain`, and writes to `/fhir-event` (see `IVG_ALLOW_FHIR_WRITES`). The Python library is unaffected.

### `IVG_REQUIRE_ARNO`

Default: unset. Read in `iris_vector_graph/_arno_gate.py`.

`1` makes the Arno reader gate fail instead of skip when the library is absent (a pre-release step).

### `IVG_SCHEMA_PREFIX`

Default: `Graph_KG`. Read in `iris_vector_graph/engine.py`, `iris_vector_graph/schema_name.py`.

The IVG Schema (the SQL schema of IVG's tables) an engine uses when `schema_prefix=` is not given. A name that cannot be one raises `IVGSchemaError` when the engine is built.

### `IVG_SNAPSHOT_DIR`

Default: the system temporary directory. Read in `iris_vector_graph/cypher_api.py`.

Where the HTTP server's `POST /admin/snapshot` writes; set it to a durable directory.

### `IVG_STRICT_NAMESPACE`

Default: unset. Read in `iris_vector_graph/stores/iris_sql_store.py`.

`1` also issues the namespace-mismatch message as a `NamespaceMismatchWarning`, so a run with warnings as errors fails on it.

### `IVG_URL`

Default: `http://localhost:8200`. Read in `iris_vector_graph/cli.py`.

The server the `ivg` command-line client talks to (`--url`).
